title: Free City of Hamburg
capsule: The Free City of Hamburg (Freie und Hansestadt Hamburg) was a sovereign city-state and one of the founding members of the German Confederation in 1815, following the Napoleonic Wars during which Hamburg had been incorporated into the French Empire as a département. As a free port positioned at the mouth of the Elbe, Hamburg functioned as the primary gateway for transatlantic trade into Central Europe, and its merchant senate governed without a monarch through an oligarchic republican constitution. The city joined the North German Confederation in 1866 and entered the German Empire as a constituent free city on 18 January 1871 at Versailles; it retained its free-port status and formal senate government under the imperial constitution, eventually becoming a full customs-union member only in 1888.
